ordered_diagnoses: Infective endocarditis of the pulmonary valve

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute presentation of severe back pain, chest pain, and episodes of light-headedness with a history of infective endocarditis and recent tricuspid valve replacement
salient_findings: Tachycardia with heart rates between 150 and 190 beats per minute
Hypotension with blood pressure 94/60 mm Hg
key_facts: Female patient in her 40s
History of infective endocarditis
History of hepatitis C
Ongoing intravenous drug use
Recent tricuspid valve replacement with a 29-mm bioprosthetic Carpentier-Edwards valve
Transient third-degree heart block after valve replacement
Pacemaker placement two days prior to current presentation
Episodes of light-headedness and chest pain after pacemaker placement
Blood pressure 94/60 mm Hg
Heart rates between 150 and 190 beats per minute
Electrocardiogram shows P waves upright in leads II, III, and aVF with sinus rate of 96 beats per minute
Grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes on electrocardiogram
Transesophageal echocardiography revealed pulmonic valve vegetations and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation secondary to a flail leaflet

raw.rationale: The patient's recent pacemaker placement and episodes of light-headedness and chest pain, combined with the electrocardiogram findings of a grouped beating pattern with 1 P wave producing 2 QRS complexes, suggest pacemaker-mediated tachycardia as the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Prosthetic valve endocarditis

rejected.why: The transesophageal echocardiography revealed pulmonic valve vegetations, but the patient's current symptoms and electrocardiogram findings are more consistent with a rhythm disturbance than a new valvular infection.
